name: Endpoint Protection Policy
description: Defines the protective measures required on endpoints and workloads, how coverage is measured, and how detections are triaged and acted upon.
purpose: Establish what protection is expected on which asset classes, and the timeframe within which detections must be acted upon, which is the benchmark for operating effectiveness.
scope_guidance: Should cover corporate endpoints, servers, and workload images, and should state explicitly whether contractor and personally owned devices are in or out of the boundary.

required_elements.element: Asset classes in scope and the protective measure expected for each
required_elements.rationale: Endpoint and immutable workload protection differ; a single expectation produces false gaps on one of them.

required_elements.element: Requirement that coverage be measured against the authoritative asset inventory
required_elements.rationale: A tool's own device list always looks complete, which is why this must be stated.

required_elements.element: Agent health and reporting expectations, not installation alone
required_elements.rationale: A non-reporting agent is functionally absent.

required_elements.element: Named responder for detections and the timeframe for triage by severity
required_elements.rationale: This becomes the commitment against which triage timeliness is assessed.

required_elements.element: Requirement to record disposition and its basis for each detection
required_elements.rationale: Distinguishes informed suppression from alerts nobody examined.

required_elements.element: Treatment of contractor and personally owned devices
required_elements.rationale: Silence here leaves coverage impossible to conclude on in either direction.

required_elements.element: Image provenance and integrity verification requirements for containerised workloads
required_elements.rationale: Usually the stronger control where workloads are ephemeral.

required_elements.element: Escalation criteria linking detections to the incident response process
required_elements.rationale: Defines when a detection stops being a triage item and becomes an incident.

required_elements.element: Named policy owner, approval record, and review cadence
required_elements.rationale: An unapproved or undated policy is treated as a documentation deficiency.

approval_expectation.approver_role: Executive accountable for security (CISO or equivalent)

communication_expectation: Communicated to IT operations, security engineering, and all endpoint users, whose device compliance the control depends on.
common_gaps: Coverage expectation stated without naming the inventory it is measured against.
No triage timeframe, so timeliness has no benchmark.
Endpoint agent expectations applied uniformly to ephemeral container workloads.
Contractor devices neither covered nor declared out of boundary.

source_refs.supports: The criteria the controls this policy documents contribute to.
The required_elements model. SOC 2 prescribes no policy contents.

notes: The criterion concerns preventing or detecting and acting upon unauthorised or malicious software. It names no product category, and this policy deliberately does not either.
